A cableway system is descending at an angle of ${45}^{∘},$ and the speed of its cabin $C$ is $10\,\text{mi/h}.$ The cabin casts a shadow $S$ vertically downwards to the ground. Assuming the angle of elevation doesn't change, find the rate at which the distance between the cableway's shadow to the landing point $L$ is decreasing.
question.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14212968/assets/4d2a9ab6bc60aa5733be4dc29aea2b03d16edbebed371963b795297a4c79a676.png)

Let $x$ be the distance from the cableway's shadow to the landing point, and let $z$ be the distance between the landing point and the cabin, as shown above.

We want to find $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}.$ To do this, let's start by setting up a relation between $x$ and $z.$ Relative to the angle $\theta ={45}^{∘},$ the sides $x$ and $z$ are the adjacent and hypotenuse, respectively. So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡({45}^{∘}) & =\frac{x}{z} \\ \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} & =\frac{x}{z} \\ x & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}z.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we differentiate both sides of the equation with respect to $t$ using implicit differentiation, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}z) \\ \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}.\end{aligned}
$$

We know that $\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}=-10\,\text{mi/h}$ (negative because the distance between the cableway's shadow and the landing point is decreasing). Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\cdot (-10)=-5\sqrt{2}.
$$

Therefore, the horizontal distance is decreasing at a rate of $5\sqrt{2}\,\text{mi/h}.$
